Messages.Author: UFOPOLI
Messages.Body:
1st Tragic Love Affair
Espoo, Finland
May 26th, 2018
2R+F
13 players, Standard constructed
Winner: Karri Malm

www.vekn.net/event-calendar/event/8893
www.facebook.com/events/232389697311256/

It was good to organize the first tournament after half a year's break caused by moving to the second biggest city in Finland, Espoo. The new location required a new title, and I decided to stick to the Toreador theme (even though "Cave of Apples" would have suited the new location).

A characteristic of this tournament was that while the games mostly weren't stagnant as such, few points were gained, and the last spot in the final was drawn between three players with 1,5 VPs (and equal TPs). Another interesting trait was the abundance of Malkavians (of both varieties), who were the main clan in at least five decks (three of which ended up in the same table in round 2).

Final RankNamePrelim GWsPrelim VPsFinal VPsTPs 1Karri Malm02390 2Jyri Puhakka01,5072 2Jani Malmi030114 2Matti Palomäki13172 2Juha Laukkanen131108 6Antti Penttilä01,572 7Petri Wessman01,572 8Jaakko Nurro01,566 9Tero Aalto0172 10Katja Jauhiainen0154 10Juho Linna0154 12Lasse Pöyry00,554 13Emma Takkunen0036

The final table:
Matti Palomäki (Lasombra/Tremere bruise bleed) Jyri Puhakka (!Malkavians with Toy) Jani Malmi (!Salubri Wall) Karri Malm (Xipe Totec toolbox) Juha Laukkanen (Malkavian bleed)

The winning deck will appear below shortly.

Messages.Author: Bloodartist
Messages.Body:
About the final decks:
Matti's deck seemed to be built around the ability to play CrimeThinc. with Thaumaturgy, giving his Lasombra/!tremere anarchs multiacting options (untap an anarch during minion phase with 1 pool). Other than that it was mostly normal dominate stuff.

Jani Malmi's !salubri wall seemed to rely heavily on the new card "righteous aura" for ousting power. Blade of Bellona was also used. Lots of flaming swords or walking sticks were waved around.

I had a single !malk in the crypt, so technically it was malk/!malk stealth bleed.

Some thoughts about the final even though I wasn't the winner:
I was first seed going into the final. I knew I didn't want to sit next to the !salubri, or in front of Matti. I knew all decks except Jyri's so I chose to be in front of Karri (who I considered the least aggressive deck of the table, a toolbox wall) and behind Matti because I was running touch of clarities and Matti was the only practical target for those.

1. Matti (dom/thaum anarchs) -> 2. Jyri (!malk + Toy) -> 3. Jani (!salubri wall) -> 4. Karri (Xipe Totec toolbox) -> 5. Juha (malk/!malk SB)

The wall decks were doing wall things on one side of table, and the other side was bleeding forward relatively aggressively. Unfortunately !salubri and Xipe Totec were too respectful of one another for my taste. I had hoped they would've hit each other more fiercely.

Jyri is suffering from strong combat of the !salubri, who are rushing mostly backwards. Matti ousts Jyri who is caught between flaming swords and multiple dominate bleed minions, then I oust Matti.
Then I get Jani into 1 pool. Ousting Jani would've afaik meant tournament victory for me, as Karri could've only gotten to even 2 points after that, and I was the first seed. Alas, my deck fails to provide stealth cards at the crucial moment and !salubri catch the winning bleed. That will be that as Karri had enough +bleed to oust me. Eventually Karri also ousts Jani for the win with about 10 minutes on the clock.

I took some pictures from the final table but unfortunately the pictures were too shaky without flash..

Smoking craters tell no tales.
—Tex talks Battletech

Messages.Author: Bloodartist
Messages.Body:
So far I haven't met anyone who was considerably upset about this tournament being unrated, although I haven't talked to Karri who won it. I guess most every participant didn't really care that much at the time of the tournament. Casual is the word.

However, I'd like to raise awareness that the information when the set is legal is hidden pretty goddamn well.

As far as I can see, the information regarding lost kindred legality is only in the header of lost kindred release, a post that I cannot even find by scrolling the forum or the front page of this site. I can see it if I follow the link given by DrnImza in this thread, but I don't actually know where it is. Its probably been buried under all the clan spoiler posts. I cant find it browsing the forum since I'm not sure where to look. The information doesn't appear anywhere else that I can see.

Browsing quickly, the information is not mentioned in the lost kindred FAQ. There was a question in the LK FAQ thread about the legality date, but it was left unanswered.

Forum search "lost kindred legal" brings up mainly this thread.

Tournament rules mention however that new releases become legal apporx. 30 days after release. Finding this rule takes some digging as well. Its however something that tournament organisers should obviously be aware of.

Jaakko said to me that he searched for the legality date from here before tournament started but couldn't find it. I can't find it right now, except for that link in this thread.

Can we, during future releases, make a clear, stickied FAQ thread that actually mentions the legality date? Lost kindred FAQ is not even stickied right now, and it doesn't even mention the date.

ps. I just did a forum search with exact phrase "Legal for tournament play" as it appears in the lost kindred release post, search can't find it. It comes up with hundred unrelated posts however.

pps. Ok I found the post. Its in Rules - Cardlists - Lost kindred. I think it should be mentioned elsewhere as well.

Perhaps in the past the judges tended to remind players of this, or I at least remember Petri sometimes having mentioned this before his tournaments.

If he knew about it and decided to let Jani play with illegal cards since he drove a long way to the tournament (at least 2 hours, or if from Joensuu then 5 and half hours) he perhaps thought that not being able to play after such a long travel would be a real bummer?

Still, the VEKN Ratings Coordinator Ankha already issued his verdict (4th post in this thread) so I think it is kinda settled.

Even it sucks big time for Karri (the winner).
